humanRead.note: The Skills and Tools tabs sit in a strip at the top of the surface, not in the window bar, and an agent is named without its harness mark. Whether an entry runs at session start follows each entry's heldBack, so an untrusted repository whose entries the daemon does not hold back reads as running, and a trusted one never says trust made it so unless no entry is held back. An entry the daemon holds back from a trusted repository, or from one that cannot be trusted, reads Held back, without until you trust this repository. A cannot-trust repository lists its refusal codes in a card the design does not draw.

Built from this inventory, not read against the design's step 18 frame. How the screen is reached is not drawn here: it opens from Open Tools on the connected machine's card on Machines. Each file card says the held-back reason once, since every entry shares it. The footer drops Trust from desktop or web where trust cannot lift the hold (a trusted repository, or one that cannot be trusted) and keeps A phone shows this but cannot trust it. Unreadable repository files, entries left out and cannot-trust reasons are listed in cards the design may draw differently. The step 16 refusal is drawn inside the start sheet that was refused (a fresh start or Start another like this one), in place of the daemon's sentence, not as a screen of its own. It uses the desktop card's wording (Domovoi did not start this session, refused · untrusted git filter, the sentence naming the drivers, It names, Nothing from the repository ran.), names each driver with its git config scope (sops · local git config) because the refusal names drivers and scopes, not files, and keeps Trust from desktop or web only where trust would lift the refusal. The Tools screen lists the repository's filter drivers under their git config file, a card that names no agent, with the source local, worktree or command-line git config. Only the git filter refusal has a code; Codex's own refusal of .codex config is still the daemon's sentence.

The card shows while the repository is untrusted and not yet reviewed and brings at least one config file the inventory lists, decided from the files and not from entries, since a file such as .codex/rules/*.rules or an empty .codex/config.toml can make an agent refuse without declaring an entry; such a file reads no entries, in the card and in the sheet. When the daemon holds back only some entries, it says how many of how many are held back and that the rest load, instead of the design's for-any-agent line, which would be false then; when it holds none back while some load, the card is titled not trusted rather than held back. Where this client cannot grant trust (a watching client), the card says Granted from desktop or web only in place of Review and trust. Since 2026-09-30 the card also lists each git config file that sets a filter driver, with its count (.git/config 1 filter driver), and a Git config not read row when the daemon could not read it, and shows for a repository whose only config is a filter; each filter command counts as one entry in the how many of how many line.

Built as a dialog over the Tools tab. A file two agents read is one group naming both agents, with each entry once. When the daemon answers config-changed, the sheet says The files changed while this was open and Nothing was trusted, which the design does not draw, and the tab reads the files again; the new digest is sent only by the next click. A cannot-trust answer lists the refusals in the sheet and removes the trust button. Env keys are counted one by one in a file's counts. When the daemon holds back only some of the repository's entries, the sheet's lead says how many of how many are held back and that the rest already load, instead of the design's None of it has run, which would be false then. When the daemon left entries out of the list, the sheet says This list is not complete, how many entries are not shown, and offers no trust until every entry can be listed, since the grant covers the whole configuration; a repository config file that could not be read blocks trust the same way, naming the file, until it can be read (ruling Q219 A). The design does not draw this state. Since 2026-09-30 each git config file and scope that sets a filter is a group of its own (path, local, worktree or command-line git config, its count), one Filter driver row per driver with each operation and its redacted command (smudge sops -d · clean sops -e), and a line the design does not draw, from ruling Q205 A: A filter driver runs its command whenever Git checks out or stages a file. If the command runs a file in this repository, it runs whatever that file holds, an agent's edit included. A git config the daemon could not read blocks trust with The repository's Git config could not be read and its reason (ruling Q219 A), and filter entries left out block it and read Git filters: N more entries were left out of this list. The pinned line counts the git config files among the files. Opened from a refused session, the sheet is the same component, reading the files when it opens. Each driver also shows its required state, which the review digest covers, in a line the design does not draw (required is true: if the filter fails, the Git command fails.). Trust sends repository.trust gitFilters with the review digest of the block it drew, only when that block lists a filter and is complete, so the daemon runs the filters (#688). A read made while the sheet is open that shows another configuration or review digest brings back The files changed while this was open, and the new digests are sent only by the next click; a refused acknowledgement reads the files again.

Read against this inventory, not the design's step 15 frame. A refused session.create closes the launcher, and a refused session.fork closes the fork dialog, and the card takes the thread lane in place of the active thread until another session, project or machine is chosen or the card's Dismiss button, which the design does not draw, is pressed. The sentence is the design's with the drivers named (and N more for drivers the daemon counted but did not name); It names lists each driver with its git config scope, not a file, because the refusal names drivers and scopes. After a grant from the card the trust clause is dropped and a line reads Trusted on the machine. Nothing has started yet., words the brief gave and the design does not draw. A refusal whose repository cannot be trusted says so and offers only Open Tools; one whose repository is trusted (a grant that did not acknowledge its git filters, or acknowledged others) says the repository is trusted, but its Git filters stay held back until they are reviewed: they were not shown when it was trusted, or they changed since, and offers Review and trust again, which opens the same sheet titled Trust the repository again. Start the session again repeats the refused request, a fork with a new request id. On a client that cannot grant trust the card says Granted from desktop or web only.
The card carries Review and trust again only; Keep held back is the sheet's button, since on the tab nothing is decided by keeping the hold.
